ov.title: Overview

ov.ruBlockedNote: No Globalping probes answered. Recheck before concluding that the address is blocked.
ov.ruStreak: Not reachable in {n} checks in a row. Consider moving the node (veiltrium export / import) or a standby address.
ov.homeStalled: transfers freeze after a few KB (TSPU cut-off)
ov.auditFailed: The action log could not be loaded.
ov.firewallMissing: The firewall rules are not loaded

cl.title: Clients
cl.subtitle: Each client has its own credentials on all three protocols. Revoking one never affects the others.
cl.select: Choose a client to see its links.
cl.qrTooLong: This link is too long for a QR code; copy it instead.
cl.awgNote: AWG Manager: add VLESS and TrustTunnel as a single server from the link; Hysteria as a server group from the JSON (it keeps the key pinning).
cl.standbyHint: Same account on {servers}; use these links as a fallback if the main address is blocked.
cl.imp.title: Import to apps
cl.imp.disabled: The client is disabled — no import data.
cl.imp.subHint: For v2rayNG, v2rayN, Happ: add a subscription from the clipboard.
cl.imp.profileHint: For Hiddify, NekoBox, Karing, sing-box SFA/SFI (sing-box 1.12 or newer): import from the clipboard or a file. The Hysteria certificate pin is checked.
cl.imp.h1: sing-box based apps (Hiddify, NekoBox, Karing, SFA, SFI): use the sing-box profile.
cl.imp.h2: Xray based apps (v2rayNG, v2rayN, Happ): use the subscription. Support for the Hysteria pin varies, so prefer VLESS Reality.
cl.imp.h3: Keenetic router (AWG Manager): VLESS and TrustTunnel by link, Hysteria through the server group JSON.
cl.imp.h4: Phones: if the connection degrades after a few minutes in VPN (TUN) mode, try proxy mode or turn off sniffing.
cl.imp.h5: Reality: set fingerprint chrome and keep TCP Fast Open off.
reset.title: Reset credentials of {name}?
reset.text: New passwords and keys are created on all three protocols. The old links and configs of {name} stop working at once, and the new ones must be sent to the person who uses them. Other clients are not affected.
reset.done: Credentials of {name} reset: send the new links
reset.failed: Not reset: {reason}. The previous credentials were kept.
add.title: Add client
add.name: Name
add.note: The three services restart: connected clients reconnect within a few seconds. Real clients check the result; on any failure the previous settings come back.
add.failed: Not added: {reason}. The previous settings were kept.
add.mainChanged: The main client's Hysteria link changed (password per client now): update it on its devices.
rm.title: Revoke {name}?
rm.text: Its Hysteria, VLESS and TrustTunnel credentials stop working at once, on every device that uses them. Other clients keep working; connected ones reconnect within seconds.
lim.why.quota: The traffic limit is used up. Raise it or wait for the counter to reset, then enable the client.
lim.why.expired: The expiry date has passed. Set a new date, then enable the client.
lim.why.manual: Disabled by you: its links do not work until you enable it.
lim.title: Limits
lim.noLimits: No limits: traffic, expiry and counter reset are not restricted.
lim.fieldLimitHint: Leave empty for no limit. Decimal units: 1 GB = 1000 MB.
lim.errLimit: Enter a positive number, at most 1 PB.
lim.fieldExpiryHint: Leave empty for no expiry. The client works through this whole day (UTC).
lim.pastWarn: This date has passed: the client will be disabled right away.
lim.fieldResetHint: When traffic counting starts again from zero (UTC; weekly: Monday, monthly: the 1st).
lim.editNote: If the client's state changes, the three services restart and are checked with real clients; on any error the previous settings come back.
lim.saveFailed: Not saved: {reason}. The previous settings are kept.
lim.disableText: The links and configs of {name} stop working right away in all three protocols, on every device. The client is kept, and you can enable it again at any time. Other clients are not affected.
lim.enableText: The links and configs of {name} work again. If the traffic limit is used up or the expiry date has passed, the server refuses: raise the limit or set a new date first.
step.check-hysteria: Check Hysteria with a real client
step.check-reality: Check VLESS Reality with a real client
common.copyManual: Automatic copying is unavailable here. Tap the field, select all and copy manually.
health.title: Connection health
health.title.unconfirmed: Services are running; your connection is not confirmed
health.title.partial: Some tunnels work; others need attention
health.title.confirmed: A tunnel worked in your network check
health.title.homeFailed: Your network check found a problem
health.title.address: Some address probes did not answer
health.detail.unconfirmed: Service status and TCP probes do not prove that VPN traffic passes through your provider.
health.detail.servicesDown: One or more enabled protocols are not active. Check the node before changing client profiles.
health.detail.firewall: The Veiltrium firewall table was not found. Diagnose the node and restore its protection.
health.detail.partial: A recent verified home-network probe succeeded on at least one protocol and reported problems on another.
health.detail.confirmed: This is a saved test result, not continuous monitoring. See its date and protocol below.
health.detail.homeFailed: A recent verified probe reported failed or interrupted transfers. A running service can still be unreachable through your provider.
health.detail.address: Globalping checks the address and TCP ports. Missing replies alone do not prove a block or test the VPN protocols.
health.action.diagnose: Run this on the server and review the reported errors:
health.action.home: Run the Keenetic probe from the network where you use the VPN and import its result on this server.
health.action.working: Use a protocol with an OK probe result. Recheck the other protocols from the same network.
health.action.connect: Connect a device with the step-by-step guide, then check browsing and a longer transfer.
health.action.russia: Repeat the address check, then test a real tunnel from your network before deciding to move the node.
health.probeHelp: Guide: README → Reference → Home-network probe. The result must have a verified route; an unchecked route is not evidence.
health.evidence: Protocols and dates of the evidence
health.expiry: Home-network evidence expires after {days} days; address probes after 12 hours.
health.probe.route_unverified: route not verified; result does not confirm VPN operation
setup.title: Connect a device
setup.appPrompt: Choose a format your app accepts
setup.app.android: VLESS link: for example, v2rayNG. Full JSON: the official sing-box for Android (SFA), or an app that explicitly supports complete sing-box profiles.
setup.app.ios: Choose VLESS for an app that supports Reality links, or full JSON for sing-box for Apple platforms (SFI). Verify the accepted format in your installed app.
setup.app.windows: VLESS links can be imported in v2rayN. Choose full JSON only if your app explicitly accepts a complete sing-box configuration.
setup.app.router: In AWG Manager add VLESS or TrustTunnel as a server by link, or import the Hysteria JSON as a server group.
setup.reason.vless: Uses Reality key verification. A single link imports this server; standby links remain in advanced connection details.
setup.reason.singbox: Includes certificate pinning, DNS and automatic selection among enabled Hysteria/Reality addresses, including configured standbys. Requires sing-box 1.12+.
setup.reason.awg: Keeps Hysteria key pinning and includes configured standby addresses.
setup.reason.tt: The server certificate is embedded in the link. AWG Manager uses TrustTunnel over HTTP/2.
setup.reason.hy2: Your app must verify pinSHA256. If it ignores the pin, use the full sing-box JSON instead.
setup.import.vless: Copy the full link or scan its QR code in your VPN app. In v2rayN use import from clipboard; in v2rayNG add a profile from the clipboard or QR.
setup.import.singbox: Download the JSON. In sing-box add a local profile from this file; keep the full configuration rather than importing it as a single outbound.
setup.import.awg: Download or copy the JSON. In AWG Manager import it as a server group, not as a Hysteria share link.
setup.import.tt: Copy the whole tt:// link. In AWG Manager add a TrustTunnel server from this link.
setup.import.hy2: Copy the link or scan the QR code. Check that the imported profile keeps and verifies the certificate pin.
setup.activate.android: Select the imported profile, connect and approve the system VPN request. Keep the Reality fingerprint set to chrome.
setup.activate.ios: Select the profile, connect and approve adding the VPN configuration when iOS asks.
setup.activate.windows: Select the profile and enable the app’s system proxy or TUN mode so browser traffic goes through it.
setup.activate.router: Enable the imported server or group and assign the devices that should use it to the appropriate routing policy.
setup.testIntro: Check from the device and network where you will actually use the VPN:
setup.opened: With the VPN connected, a site that needs the tunnel opens.
setup.transfer: A download larger than 1 MB completes without freezing.
setup.testNote: These checkboxes are your confirmation in this browser tab. The panel does not measure your device’s route or connection.
setup.done: You confirmed browsing and a longer transfer. The device setup is complete.
setup.troubleText: Check the client is enabled, reimport its current credentials, then try another enabled protocol. For a frozen transfer use the home-network probe; for an unavailable address check the standby state before switching.
setup.advanced: All links, QR codes and advanced import formats
sb.title: Standby state
sb.scope: Signed snapshots compare credentials, certificates, ports and client restrictions. They do not test reachability or synchronize servers. A match is valid for 24 hours from the snapshot.
sb.none: No standby addresses configured. Set STANDBY_HOSTS when running the installer after preparing copies of this node.
sb.how2: Paste its complete vt-standby-1|… line below. Both nodes need this version of the script and the shared probe key from the same node export.
sb.how3: After a credential, client, limit or port change, compare again. Local changes are detected against stored snapshots immediately on refresh.
sb.recorded: Snapshot verified and saved. Review the comparison for its address.
sb.thisReceipt: This server’s receipt for another node
sb.receiptNote: Contains no passwords or keys. It is authenticated with the shared probe key and describes saved configuration, not a live tunnel test. Generate a new receipt after changing configuration.
sb.noReceipt: No receipt is available. Check the installed script version, public IPv4 address and probe key.
sb.updateText: On the primary run veiltrium export /root/node-backup.enc, copy the encrypted archive to the standby and run bash veiltrium.sh --import /root/node-backup.enc there. Keep the passphrase separate. Imports keep the node’s shared credentials; then generate a new receipt on the standby and verify it here. Reimport updated client profiles if ports or server names changed.
sb.quotaNote: Traffic counters and quota enforcement are local to each server. Matching restrictions do not create a shared traffic allowance; timers may change client state independently.
sb.changeWarning: This changes only this server. Standbys {servers} are independent: old credentials may keep working there after revoke, disable or reset. Update each copy and verify a new snapshot. Traffic quotas are per server.
